title: Oncall Flow DSL & Lightweight Playbook Runner for Admin Support Automation
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Problem: Oncall engineers and support staff currently run ad-hoc shell snippets and scattered runbooks during incidents. This creates inconsistent remediation, long mean time to mitigate (MTTM), and poor auditability. Goal: Deliver a small, audited playbook runner and a concise Oncall Flow DSL that lets SREs and support create parameterized task flows (check, fix, escalate) as first-class tasks that can be executed from Slack, Console, or the admin CLI. The runner must be lightweight, sandboxed, observable, and integrate with existing admin utilities (opsctl) and runbooks-as-tasks inventory. Deliverables: 1) Simple Oncall Flow DSL spec and reference parser, 2) A Playbook Runner service (stateless control plane + ephemeral runners) with RBAC, KMS-encrypted secrets support, and event logging to Console, 3) Admin CLI + Slack command extensions to trigger flows, 4) Migration guide and a small set of canonical playbooks (DB failover, queue pump restart, EVN cache warm). Acceptance criteria: - Authoring a 10-step flow in DSL under 10 minutes with examples, - Execution latency < 800ms for simple checks, end-to-end runbook step audit entries in Console, - RBAC enforcement so only SREs or assigned oncall rotations can run escalation steps, - Postmortem includes playbook effectiveness metrics for at least two incidents during the pilot.
acceptance_criteria: DSL authoring doc with examples published to Confluence (how-to + lint rules)
Playbook Runner deployed to staging and exerciseable via opsctl and Slack integration
Audit logs emitted to Console with step-level timestamps and user identity for all executed flows
RBAC checks enforced via existing SSO groups; unauthorized attempts are rejected and logged
Secrets used by flows must be retrieved via KMS-backed vault and never rendered in logs
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Initial spike completed; prototype DSL grammar (YAML-inspired but strict verbs) in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/tree/eng-912345/spike
2025-02-18: Design review with SREs and Support team. Key feedback: prefer idempotent steps and built-in dry-run mode. Added step-level retry policy concept.
2025-02-20: Security sync: confirmed KMS integration approach; Vault wrappers to be implemented by infra team. Security requested a threat model and code scan prior to staging deploy.
2025-02-24: MVP runner skeleton implemented (HTTP API + agentless executor). Demoed basic flow execution with synthetic DB-failcheck. Measured average step exec time ~220ms for simple check.
2025-02-26: Added Slack slash-command prototype; needs rate-limit and cooldown to avoid accidental mass runs. Filed follow-up task ENG-912346 for rate-limit implementation.
2025-02-28: Paused on adding native shell-run steps until sandboxing is validated by Security. Moving forward with built-in primitives (http_check, pg_query, restart_service) for MVP.
decisions: DSL format: YAML-like but restricted verbs to reduce authoring errors and simplify parser (chosen over full JSON schema for readability)
Execution model: control-plane triggers ephemeral runner containers that pull flow and secrets; chosen over embedded server-side execution to reduce blast radius
Sandboxing: MVP will expose a curated set of safe primitives (no raw shell execution) to meet Security requirements; raw command execution gated behind a separate approval flow
State & audit: all step outputs (redacted) and statuses will be sent to Console's events pipeline and linked to the incident id
Secrets: flows reference secret keys; vault access uses short-lived tokens issued by Running Runner role via KMS; secrets never logged in plaintext

Runner images must be minimal and scanned; prefer Go binary + static assets to avoid runtime CVEs
